title: Poetry Adventure 2 · Analysing Poems

concepts.def: A turn or shift in a poem's thought
Repeating a word at the start of lines
Words that nearly but don't fully rhyme

walkthroughs.body_html:
Shelley's sonnet ends: "Nothing beside remains."

The harsh caesura after "remains" leaves emptiness on the page — mirroring the empty desert and mocking the tyrant's ego.

Owen's plosives in Exposure ("merciless iced east winds that knive us") make the cold feel physical.

Soft sibilance in love poems creates intimacy. Always link sound to feeling.

A volta is the turn — where the poem changes direction. In sonnets it's often at line 9.

Identifying it shows the examiner you understand the poem's emotional arc.

caesura
sonnet
plosive
plosive
sibilance
anaphora
enjambment

mcqs.q: What is the structure of a Shakespearean sonnet?
options: A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
A sonnet is any short love poem.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
Fourteen lines in iambic pentameter, structured as three quatrains and a final couplet, rhyming ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, often with a volta near the couplet.
The claim that judging a text by what the author 'intended' is fallacious — the text's meaning lies in the work itself, not the author's stated or guessed intentions.
A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
It means authors can never make mistakes when writing.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.

mcqs.q: What did Romantic poets value in nature?
options: A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
Romantic poets just liked to write about pretty landscapes.
Nature as a source of spiritual insight and emotional truth, accessed through imagination — not picturesque scenery for its own sake.
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.
